answer_1.quote: Common n-gram metrics such as BLEU and ROUGE are often not well correlated with human judgments for many natural language generation (NLG) tasks such as machine translation, summarization, and dialogue.

answer_2.quote: We compare the performance of mt5 SEAHORSE to several baselines: • majority_class A majority class baseline (i.e., picking the most frequent class). • ROUGE-L The ROUGE-L score between the article and the summary.

answer_3.quote: We finetune mT5_xxl with the SEAHORSE training set to do this task, finetuning a separate metric for each dimension of quality. We call this model mt5 SEAHORSE.

answer_4.quote: For each summary, we collect annotations along 6 dimensions, also referred to as Q1-6: Q1 comprehensible: The summary can be read and understood by the rater. (If 'No,' the rest of the questions will be skipped.) Q2 repetition: The summary is free of unnecessarily repeated information. Q3 grammar: The summary is grammatically correct. Q4 attribution: All the information in the summary is fully attributable to the source article. Q5 main ideas: The summary captures the main idea(s) of the source article. Q6 conciseness: The summary concisely represents the information in the source article.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators answer six questions (Q1-Q6) about the summary, with Q1-Q3 without the article and Q4-Q6 with the article. They answer 'Yes', 'No', or 'Unsure'.
